Two call sites — that's the "noticing" stage, not the "build it" stage. Rule of Three: I don't pull something into a shared helper until it's shown up a third time. Right now we've got two data points, which isn't enough to know what the actual shape of the abstraction should be — retry-with-backoff for one call site might need different backoff params, different exception handling, different max-retry logic than the other. Guessing at a shared shape now risks building the wrong generalization.

What I'd do instead: name it out loud (which you just did), and leave a note somewhere visible — comment, ticket, whatever — so when a third one shows up, whoever writes it knows to check for the pattern instead of copy-pasting again. If the third one does land, then we design the helper against three real examples instead of two plus a guess.

If there's a concrete third call site already on the horizon — not hypothetical, actually planned — that changes the math and I'd reconsider. Is there one, or is it just these two so far?
